name: LazyGrid
declaration: public struct LazyGrid<Data: RandomAccessCollection, ID: Hashable, Content: View>: View
abstract: A vertically scrolling, equal-column grid that constructs only visible rows plus overscan. Row heights are explicit so scrolling never measures the full collection. Stable item identities preserve overlapping cells. Row heights and row spacing are authored logical values and follow TextScaler once. Row state that must survive leaving the viewport belongs in the model.
discussion:
With `columnWidth` the grid is wider than its viewport: it scrolls on both
axes and also constructs only the visible columns. `columnSpan` lets an
item cover several columns; rows are packed in order, and an item that does
not fit the rest of a row starts the next one.

edge to edge: the app paints its background behind the system bars and only
its interactive chrome is inset. `SafeArea` consumes the insets this root
publishes, so screens that own a status bar, navigation bar or keyboard get
the correct avoidance without a letterboxed surface.

cannot drift from what a real surface renders.

name: VirtualStack
declaration: public struct VirtualStack<Data: RandomAccessCollection, ID: Hashable, Content: View>: View
abstract: A vertically scrolling stack that constructs only the rows around the viewport. Row identity survives scrolling; keep persistent row data in the model, since fully offscreen rows are unmounted. IDs must be unique.
discussion:
Pass a constant `rowHeight` for uniform rows, a closure for known
variable heights, or `estimatedRowHeight` when heights are only known
after rendering. The closure receives the element, the available content
width and the inherited text scaler, and returns the complete row height;
heights are cached until data, width, spacing or text scale change, and
scrolling locates rows in O(log n). `preload` adds a fraction of the
viewport across both edges (0.3 prepares about 130%); `overscan` is the
minimum extra row count per edge. Refill happens before that buffer runs out.

name: ZStack
abstract: Layer children in declaration order. The last child is painted and hit first; earlier children remain mounted and keep their state.

name: ZStackLayout
abstract: Layered container. Children are measured against the available proposal and placed on top of each other in declaration order: the last child paints on top and receives pointer input before earlier children.
discussion:
The stack itself measures to its largest child. It does not clip; overflow
remains painted and hit-testable unless the caller applies `.clipped()`.
